extracted.intended_audience: educated lay readers interested in natural philosophy and theology (readers of The Religious Philosopher)
extracted.subtask_description: An early-modern essay presenting natural-philosophical observations (astronomy, mechanics, microscopy) as reasons to recognize divine power and providence; combines empirical measurements, comparative reasoning, and large-number calculations to persuade readers. The page lists the specific considerations and experimental demonstrations the author uses to support theological conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare one thing with another to judge arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: to gain a true Notion of the Planetary Heavens familiar to them, and comparing one thing with another, to consider whether a Man argues without Foundation, who maintains, that the Power and Wisdom of the Great Creator shines out more brightly here than the Skill and Contrivance of the Workman in the most curious Clock, or any other Machine whatsoever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparative reasoning between natural systems and human artifacts to test whether claiming divine perfection from nature is reasonable; the reader is urged to form clear conceptions of the heavens and then compare features to human workmanship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the immense magnitudes and distances of the planets
rubrics_metrics.description: First, considering the almost unconceivable Magnitude of these wandering Globes, and their Distances from the Sun, which may only and easily be determined by the Diameters of the Earth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use geometrical/astronomical measures (e.g., Earth-diameter units) to establish scale; emphasize enormity as evidence of a supreme directing power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe gravitational attraction without physical connection
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondly, seeing that Saturn, tho' it be distant from the Sun at near 100,000 of the said Diameters, between every two following Points of its Orbit, is always attracted towards the Sun, notwithstanding there is not the least Band or Connexion between the one Body and the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out that attraction acts across vast distances without mechanical contact; treat this as remarkable and indicative of governing force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note that perihelion approaches occur for all planets
rubrics_metrics.description: Thirdly, Finding that these Approaches to the Sun have place in all the Planets, though there is likewise no Union between any of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize universality of the phenomenon across planetary bodies as strengthening the inference of orderly direction rather than chance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each planet moves in its own particular plane
rubrics_metrics.description: Fourthly, Knowing that each of them performs its Course in a particular Plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stress the geometrical regularity (distinct orbital planes) as part of the ordered system to be explained; use this regularity against the notion of mere randomness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planets move in ellipses preserving geometric properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Fifthly, That they describe no Circles which we see generated in natural Motions, after different manners, but to shew that a particular Direction obtains here, they move in Ellipses, or oval Figures, every where Preserving their Geometrical Properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight that orbital shape (ellipses) is a consistent geometric property; treating geometric regularity as evidence of directed design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aphelia of ellipses point to different places in heavens
rubrics_metrics.description: Sixthly, that these oval Figures are each of them extended lengthwise to a different Place in the starry Heavens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out that the remote points (aphelia) of different planets are not all aligned but point to different parts of the sky—used to argue against a simple mechanical or unified accidental cause and for a higher will arranging them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability and long duration of planetary motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Seventhly, That their Motions have continued for many Ages in this Order, without any Confusion among each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the long-term stability and lack of confusion in planetary orbits as a criterion for inferring consistent direction and governance over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine enormous size with prodigious speed as astounding
rubrics_metrics.description: And, Finally, since no body who understands it-right, can, without Amazement, observe, That these Globes of such an amazing Magnitude ... and yet all of 'em move about the Sun with so prodigious a Swiftness, as far exceeds that of a Cannon Bullet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ striking quantitative contrasts (huge mass vs. great velocity) and comparisons to familiar measures (e.g., 'cannon-bullet' speed) to impress the reader and support theological awe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use observed axial rotations as empirical facts to compute velocities
rubrics_metrics.description: we find ... that the Sun turns round upon its own Axis in 25 Days; Venus in 23; Mars in 24½; and the great Globe of Jupiter in 10 Hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on observed rotations (of sun and planets) together with assumed diameters to calculate equatorial speeds as part of the demonstration of extraordinary natural forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on experiments and measurements (Boyle, Huygens, Leuwenhoek)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Truth of this may be seen in all the Books of the Astronomers, and particularly the Places of the Aphelia of each in the Automaton of Mr. Huygens ... we will lay down for a Foundation, the Experiments of Mr. Leuwenhoek ... Mr. Boyle ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor philosophical/theological claims in the contemporary experimental literature; cite experimental demonstrations and trusted authorities as foundations for inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ quantitative calculations and analogies to convey scale
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to convince every one of the Dreadfulness of the Powers which exert themselves in this Matter, we need only investigate the Swiftness wherewith these great Globes are carried ... For supposing the Earth's Diameter ... the Circumference thereof will contain ... Now each Point that is upon the Surface of the Earth at the Equator would run so many Fathoms in 24 Hours ... But a Cannon Bullet ... runs 100 of the like Fathoms in a Second.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use step-by-step numerical reckoning (diameters, circumferences, times) and analogies to common experiences (bullets, clocks) to make abstract magnitudes intelligible and persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate minuteness and multitude of particles as evidence of providence
rubrics_metrics.description: Let us moreover ... Of the Unspeakable Number, and Unconceivable Smallness of the Particles of which the Universe consists ... That all visible Bodies do consist of an unconceivable Number of such little Parts ... A Cubical Inch contains a Million of visible Particles ... a Drop of Water is divisible into above 26,000,000 Parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue from micro-scale complexity (huge numbers of minute particles in liquids, air, light) to the necessity of wisdom and providential direction; perform explicit estimates and experiments to make the point concrete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use microscopic observations to extend the argument across scales
rubrics_metrics.description: This Hypothesis founded upon the Observations of Mr. Leuwenhoek, namely, That a Drop of Water contains many more than one Million Millions of Parts; the same applicable to all kinds of Liquids ... he distinguished in Pepper-Water ... three sorts of Animalcula of different Sizes ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate microscopy findings (animalcula, tiny bubbles) as empirical evidence for extreme minuteness and multiplicity; then relate these microfacts to macro-inferences about the universe and divine ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invoke the astonishment of the reasonable atheist as a rhetorical criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Before we proceed any farther, let an Atheist stop a little here, and consider with us, how great and how penetrating that Providence and Direction must be, which before a Drop of Rain Water ... has thought fit to compound it of so many Millions of Parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the reaction ('amazement') of a thoughtful doubter as a rhetorical test: if empirical facts produce astonishment, they serve as persuasive grounds for acknowledging providence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt epistemic modesty: present figures as far as experience permits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reader must not expect to meet here with an exact Description of the Figures thereof, forasmuch as without ever being thoroughly fathomed or comprehended, they will always furnish new Matter of Inquiry to learned Men ... We shall therefore only consider some Matters and Bodies with respect to their Smallness, not perhaps so thoroughly as the accurate Truth of the Thing may require, but only so far as Experience may lead us therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit claims to what experiment and observation will support; acknowledge remaining uncertainty and avoid over-precise speculative descriptions when evidence is lacking.
